review_notes: I read the whole file. It has no simp lemmas or attributes of its own. It declares one Prop-valued abbrev, several transport theorems and instances, and a few iff characterisations. Its only simp uses are `by simp` and `by simp [Q]` inside `krullDim_Icc`. The iff theorems such as `isCatenary_iff_height_add` are proved by `rw`, and they are not good simp rules anyway. They restate a predicate with new hypotheses, and some have binder-instance hypotheses. The `krullDim_Icc` equation is a possible rewrite, but it changes `krullDim` of a set into a quotient `height`. That is not an obviously canonical normal form, so I do not recommend a simp attribute. I did not check how TauCeti/Order/Catenary.lean treats simp, and I did not run Lean. I found no justified simp-interface defect.
